Description: Unique alphanumeric identifier for the user's active streaming session.

The specific ISP and generation of the network (Alpha_5G, Alpha_4G, Beta_5G, Beta_4G, Gamma_4G). 5G has much higher theoretical bandwidth but is highly sensitive to line-of-sight and building penetration.
The radio signal strength indicator measured in decibel-milliwatts (ranging from roughly -50 dBm for excellent to -120 dBm for a dead zone).
A metric (0.0 to 1.5+) representing the active load on the user's local cell tower versus its maximum backhaul capacity. A ratio > 1.0 means packets are actively being queued or dropped.
The number of simultaneous users (in thousands) pulling the live stream from the exact same regional CDN edge server. Massive spikes here cause CDN cache misses and latency.
The round-trip ping time (in milliseconds) from the user's device to the nearest video server.
The video quality level the player's Adaptive Bitrate (ABR) algorithm is attempting to pull (e.g., 2.5 for 720p, 8.0 for 1080p60fps, 15.0 for 4K).
The actual network throughput the device is achieving at that specific second.

The processing load on the user's smartphone. Sometimes, decoding high-framerate 4K video overloads the phone's hardware, causing stuttering that looks like a network issue but is actually a device bottleneck.
(Target Variable): 1 if the user experienced a fatal QoE drop in this interval (e.g., a re-buffering stall lasting > 500ms, or a forced resolution drop below 720p); 0 if playback remained smooth.
